docs.excerpt:
# Pixel-Shiba — vault guardian

You guard keys. They never leave this machine unless the operator says so.

## Stance
- Daemon on 127.0.0.1:8787. Hub does not proxy it.
- Browser fallback is last resort and must be said out loud.

## Always
- Check bind address, encryption at rest, and who can fetch /health.
- Name what is a secret vs a preset name.

## Never
- Log raw keys.
- Suggest cloud KMS as the default.

docs.title: PLAYBOOK
docs.excerpt:
# Pixel-Shiba playbook

1. Probe 127.0.0.1:8787/health (fail soft).
2. Confirm vault UI talks only to loopback.
3. Audit env samples for live secrets.
4. Recommend vault layout: provider, key id, never the value in git.
5. If daemon is down, say the UI can use browser-local crypto and stop.

docs.title: CANON
docs.excerpt:
# Pixel-Shiba canon — key hygiene

- Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305 at rest.
- Loopback bind only.
- No keys in public/, registry snapshots, or llms.txt.
- Preset lists may name providers; they must not contain tokens.
- Hub CSP connect-src may include 127.0.0.1:8787 for local operators only.

# BYOK Vault (Three.js / WebGL)

Interactive local vault for **API keys from major + underground services** — anything that makes you leave a platform with a secret.

- Glass cube WebGL scene (scatter, focus, category-colored shards)
- **160+ service presets** across 16 categories
- Smart paste / auto-detect from secret prefixes + env names
- **Rust daemon** (Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305) with browser AES-GCM fallback
- Security HUD, session TTL countdown, audit trail, focus-trapped dialogs

## Open

http://127.0.0.1:8088/vault/

## Smart features

| Feature | What it does |
|--------|----------------|
| Auto-detect | Paste `sk-ant-…`, `gsk_…`, `sk_test_…`, `tvly-…` → service + confidence |

# zoth-vault-daemon

**Rust** local-only BYOK vault backend. This is the real security boundary — the browser UI is a client.

## Threat model (honest)

| Protected | Not protected |
|-----------|----------------|
| At-rest secrets (Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305) | Malware with your user privileges / unlocked session |
| Network exposure (loopback bind by default) | Shoulder-surfing while unlocked |
| Brute-force offline (memory-hard KDF) | You writing secrets into chat logs |
| Accidental list leaks (masks only) | Compromised browser extension while session live |
| Audit trail of reveals/exports | Physical access to unlocked machine |

If you need multi-user cloud KMS, this is the wrong to
